text:
eli: Heads-up — customer on dedicated-prod-5 hitting bursts of 429s + high p95 latency (~2s+) since 08:10 UTC. They say most requests are long-chat sessions (~8k-12k tokens). Ticket INC-4219.
ajay: Got it. Tenant id? sample request IDs? Is this only dedicated-prod-5 or across other pools?
eli: tenant_id=redwood-thermo. A few req ids: r12345, r12346. Confirmed only on dedicated-prod-5 (same region). Customer reported spikes align with heavy multi-turn threads.
devon: pulled kvcache metrics for the pool — eviction rate and slab ops spiked at the same time as the 429s. Snippet:

```
kvcache.evictions.count  3200
kvcache.kb.used          12.4GB
kvcache.slab_compactions 47
kvcache.fragmentation_pct 18.7
```

sam: Autoscaler didn't add nodes. Looks like we were in cooldown/backoff from prior churn; min=2 max=8 cooldown=300s. So throughput headroom unavailable when the long-context workload ramped.
ajay: Can we get a representative request payload to repro locally? Also run `rwdctl pool metrics --pool=dedicated-prod-5 --series=kvcache.* --range=15m` and paste results.
eli: sample curl (redacted creds):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-4x","context": [<~10k tokens>], "max_tokens": 800}'
```

eli: Pasted trimmed `rwdctl` output to Gist (link) — shows sharp eviction + slow reclaim.
ops-bot: ALERT: kvcache.evictions.rate > threshold for pool dedicated-prod-5 at 2026-03-15T08:10:22Z :alarm_clock:
devon: Root cause hypothesis: long-context requests blow up KV cache footprint, causing fragmentation and heavy compaction; eviction storms then starve runtime leading to request throttling. The autoscaler couldn't react because of backoff and sustained allocation failures.
ajay: Agreed. Two parallel actions: 1) short-term mitigation for customer (reduce max_context / enable per-tenant max_entries), 2) infra changes to reduce cooldown or temporary burst capacity. Also need to reproduce on staging.
sam: Filed INFRA-1298 to provision a temporary extra node in pool and to lower cooldown to 60s for canary. Also adding an automatic fallback policy to route long-context workloads to a lower-QPS model variant.
devon: Trying quick config change to enable prefix-based eviction and lower kvcache.max_entries_per_tenant to 50k for this tenant only (targeted QoS). Will patch via feature-flag so we can rollback.
ajay: When you flip the flag, capture `metrics.kvcache.latency_p95` and `http.429.rate` before/after. If 429s drop and p95 improves, schedule a controlled rollout.
eli: Customer notified — asked them to throttle clients to 6k tokens as a stopgap. They accepted temporary mitigation.
devon: Patch applied to dedicated-prod-5 for tenant redwood-thermo at 08:42 UTC: enabled prefix eviction + tenant max_entries=50k. Monitoring now.
ops-bot: NOTE: config-change recorded: kvcache.prefix_eviction=on for tenant redwood-thermo @ 2026-03-15T08:42:05Z
ajay: Early numbers: eviction rate down 65%, compaction ops down, 429s reduced to baseline. Still watching for fragmentation tail.
sam: Plan: next 24h keep prefix-eviction on, run a compaction-tune job in off-peak, and schedule a controlled autoscaler cooldown change in canary pool tomorrow.
eli: Thanks team — I'll close the loop with the customer and update INC-4219 with the remediation steps and timeline. Leaving thread open for further follow-up.
devon: Logged repro notes and sample scripts to the internal playbook: `playbooks/repro-kvcache-longctx.md`. Will try to create a compact unit test to simulate multi-turn token growth.
ajay: Also add an alert to detect "kvcache.fragmentation_pct > 15% + sustained eviction > 500/min" so we can catch next time before 429s spike.
eli: :thumbsup:
